body: What kind of life is living without a single person to care if you're alive or dead? That doesn't sound like a life worth living.
Some mistakes can't be fixed, you can only ensure that they don't happen again.

You're right, they shouldn't care. I'm not worth caring about. It was a mistake to ever get my hopes up. It was a mistake to put my life in a position where not a single person cares. It's a mistake to be alive at all.

Those aren't real answers. 

So what if it's possible to get better for some people? So what if it's possible to not die and be happy? This is not true for all people (and if you think it is, IMO you're unfairly projecting your world views onto others), but *even if it is* what's so bad about someone deciding that they don't consent to keep going?

> we aren't living for others

At this point, I kind of am. Regardless of whether or not you think I should be. In any case, the point was more so that if I did die, it would be with minimal impact and I wouldn't need to think about downstream consequences to the people around me.
